subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should OpenClaw make `chat.send` ACK contingent on durable user-turn visibility/progress for WebChat, or keep the current faster ACK plus UI-side preservation and post-dispatch fallback model?
rationale: Both choices are plausible product/runtime contracts, and the safer durable boundary may change latency and duplicate/session-rollover behavior beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Adopt durable progress contract
options.body: Rework or replace the gateway candidate so accepted WebChat sends are durably visible or visibly failed, with tests for duplicate sends, session rollover, and runtime-owned persistence.

options.title: Keep fast ACK contract
options.body: Document that `started` only means accepted for dispatch and rely on UI pending preservation plus follow-up fixes for remaining silent-failure modes.

options.title: Close as UI-fixed only
options.body: Treat the current pending-send/history preservation as sufficient and close the durable transcript concern without changing gateway semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt durable progress contract
recommendation.body: Rework or replace the gateway candidate so accepted WebChat sends are durably visible or visibly failed, with tests for duplicate sends, session rollover, and runtime-owned persistence.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the user-turn transcript recorder and persistence contract introduced in their recent merged refactor.
